recipes.name: Simple Artichoke Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Mix artichoke hearts, mayonnaise, and Parmesan cheese together in a bowl until well combined.
Spread mixture in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and golden brown, about 15 to 20 minutes.

Serve and enjoy! Believe it or not, you’ll need just three ingredients for this easy artichoke dip recipe: a can of artichoke hearts, mayonnaise, and Parmesan cheese. Of course, you can customize the ingredients or spice it up however you like.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is the perfect base for any hot artichoke dip. Make it just the way it is 1-1-1 or mix it up with some chopped jalepenos, spinach, green peppers or roasted garlic. Depending on the crowd I serve it to, I adjust it accordingly. The only downfall, there's never enough. When making for a crowd make a quadruple batch at least. It even works in the crock pot.

I have been making this exact recipe (and slight variations) since I was a teenager. My mom felt we should have a few recipes to be able to quickly and easily whip up by memory for when we get invited to someone's house (never arrive empty handed). I've passed that on to my kids. It becomes greasier the more you cook it, so cook until warm inside and if you want the bubbly crust, put it under the broiler to finish. I blend 1/2 of the artichokes in a processor with some of the mayo, and chop the rest into smaller pieces. Some variations I have used: splash of lemon juice, chopped spinach, chopped caramelized onion, roasted garlic, and sun-dried tomatoes. Use add-ins sparingly. Drain the artichokes well and blot dry. I only use Hellman's (aka Best Foods). You'll need to make a double batch if you are taking it to a party- it will go that fast. IF there are any leftovers, spread it on bread and toast under the broiler.

The taste of this is far above any I've had before, including several restaurants! ( I did add 1 tablespoon of garlic I bought in a jar). The texture made it a little hard to dip so I melted some grated cheddar-gruyere cheese on top. That was a mistake because when trying to spoon or dip some out, the whole top layer of melted cheese tried to come along. Next time, I'll mix in some spinach and grated or cream cheese before baking. It is SO good! I lined my pan with parchment so I could easily remove and freeze half but the two of us ate more than half, then decided we should just go ahead and eat the rest the next day. LOL

I have made this many times as well as other rifs on this theme. The addition of ceram cheese, blue cheese, and garlic is a show stopper as is the addition of fresh crab meat. Put a tsp + in miniature heated Phyllo cups . I use the ones made by Athena.

Great dip for sure! The original recipe comes from the 1980’s with diced Ortega chiles ( small can). Which gives it a bit of tangy flavor. I think your pan size is a bit off. That is not what the pic shows. But I think it’s a no brainer for the average cook. I would never add spinach to this dip 🤮 Note: cook it in the oven so the top gets all crispy. That’s the best part.

I haven't made this version. People who want to freeze any leftovers may want to add cream cheese or neufchatel and half the mayonnaise. It tends to separate when freezing, whereas cream cheese doesn't! Also this dip screams,cries, begs for garlic! You can use garlic powder or fresh minced . To make this quickly, put all ingredients in a blender (EXCEPT the artichoke hearts!!) Cream cheese should be room temp and cut into pieces. Hellmans is the best mayonnaise so don't skimp, just buy a small jar or squeeze bottle. Blend well and place in a baking dish then add the peeled apart artichoke hearts folding into the mixture. I peel the hearts to distribute them throughout the dip. Cutting them into pieces results in you " hunting" for the artichokes and just getting dip! Yes, you can add spinach, but for a different green and texture I used romaine lettuce. Next time I plan to try escarole. Both have zero bitter unlike spinach and are just as healthy if not more! Hope you like my versions and feel free to leave polite comments after you try. I didnt provide measurements as the recipe already has them. I assume this recipe can serve 2-3 people so increase amounts based on number of people.

I have made this several times, adding albacore tuna to the mix and topping the mixture with panko bread crumbs. I noticed that someone tried this in a 9x13 pan; it works best with a small, shallow baking dish that can go from oven to table, served with fresh baguette, tortilla chips, or crackers.
Added two drained cans of crab meat, a bunch of spinach, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Delicious.
we add 1 can drained green chilies, mild to this recipe, the mid size can. We have brought this to many events and people always rave about it. Serve with frito scoops

I've been making this recipe for years. And whenever I take it somewhere I always get asked for the recipe! The only thing I add to it is 2 cups mild finely shredded cheddar cheese. I mix 1 cup in the mix then put 1 C on top ( you can never have too much cheese!). And cook as the directions say to. Then broil until the cheese is a little browned. However, bc of the added cheese & mayo it does get a little oily. So when it cools just a little I hold the top and drain out the excess.

This is a bland version of what should be a very tasty dip. Just add 1 package of shredded mozzarella (2 cups) and 2 teaspoons garlic powder to this recipe and you'll have creamy, garlicky perfection.
I love this recipe because it doesn’t use sour cream or cream cheese. I always add garlic.
I made this for a Friendsgiving gathering and it was a hit. I did add minced garlic & a little shredded mozzarella to the recipe.

This is a great dip to make for parties. Or home. The directions say to put in a 9x13 pan to bake. There isn't enough in the single recipe to fill that size pan, so I adapted down to a size that fit better. Mmmm. Like how simple this is to make!

I have made some additions to this recipe. 1 can bits and stems mushrooms, 1 7 oz can green chilis, and also 1 small can diced jalapenos. chop everything nice and small. For tailgate tomorrow I added canned chopped habaneros as I could not find any diced "hot" jalapenos. Everywhere i take this I go with an empty dish. I usually serve with Fristos Scoops, they are nice and firm to pick up all the extras I put in.
Too easy to not make all the time! Delish! Friends raved! It’s definitely on repeat
Easy great recipe. We added a few cloves of garlic, substituted Greek yogurt for the mayo, and sprinkled seasoned panko on top. It's was gone in minutes!
